title: Apps and Public Wi-Fi
about: Choose what apps can use, and stay safe on public Wi-Fi.

cards.prompt: Apps ask to use parts of your phone, like the camera, microphone or your location. Each one is an [[app permission]]. Does the app **need** it for its job?
cards.explanation: Allow what fits the app's job: location for maps, the microphone for calls, photos for a photo editor. A torch app needs your light. It doesn't need to know who your aunt is.
cards.hint: For each one, ask: could the app do its main job without it?
cards.nudge: Think about what each app is for. A permission that has nothing to do with that job isn't needed.

cards.title: Only what it needs
cards.body:
- Allow what an app needs for **its job**. Say no to the rest.
- For location, pick **"Only while using the app"** instead of "Always". Then the app can't see where you are while it's closed.
- Changed your mind? Switch any permission off in **Settings**.

cards.prompt: You install a new drawing game.

steps.text: It asks: **"Allow access to your contacts?"** then **"Allow location: Always?"** What do you do?

choices.text: Allow both, so the game works
choices.consequence: A drawing game doesn't need your contacts or where you are, all the time.

choices.text: Say no to both, and see if the game still works
choices.consequence: It does. You can always change it later in Settings if a feature really needs it.

cards.explanation: Say no to permissions an app doesn't need. If an app **won't work at all** without permissions that have nothing to do with its job, choose a different app.
cards.hint: Would a drawing game need your contacts, or your location all the time?

cards.prompt: A weather app asks for your location. Which choice gives it what it needs for your local forecast, **and no more**?

options.text: Only while using: it gets your town when you open it
Always: the forecast is only right if it tracks you all day
options.nudge: The forecast only matters when you look at it. Does the app need to know where you go while it's closed?

options.text: Never: a weather app has no use for your location at all
options.nudge: A local forecast does use where you are. The question is how much of the time it needs to know.

cards.explanation: **"Only while using the app"** gives the weather app your location when you check the forecast, and not while it's closed. "Always" lets it follow you all day, which is more than it needs. ("Never" works too if you're happy to type your town in.)
cards.hint: When do you actually need the forecast for where you are?

cards.prompt: Many phones show a small **dot** at the top of the screen while an app is using the microphone or camera. You're reading on your phone, and a **microphone dot** appears.

steps.text: You're not on a call or recording anything. What do you do?

choices.text: Check which app is using the microphone, and switch its permission off
choices.consequence: Your phone shows which app it is. You turn its microphone permission off in Settings.
The dot means an app is listening right now. It's worth a quick check.

choices.text: Restart the phone, then carry on as normal
choices.consequence: The dot may go for now, but the app still has permission and could listen again later.

cards.explanation: The dot shows an app is using the **microphone**. Find out which app, and switch that permission off if it doesn't need it.
cards.hint: The dot means some app is using the microphone. Where can you stop an app using it for good?

cards.prompt: **Public Wi-Fi** at a café or library is shared with strangers. Most sites already scramble what you send. But you can't always be sure a network is the real one, so use **mobile data** for money and important accounts. Sort each one.
cards.explanation: Everyday browsing is fine on public Wi-Fi. For banking or important accounts, **mobile data** is safer, because you can't always be sure a network is the real one.
cards.hint: Which activities involve your money or your most important accounts?
cards.nudge: Save banking and important account changes for mobile data. Videos, news and recipes are fine.

cards.prompt: Anyone can set up a **fake hotspot**: a Wi-Fi network named to look like the café's. So ask staff for the real network's name. You're at a café. Which is the **riskiest**?

options.text: Join "Free Cafe WiFi 2" when staff don't know it
Read the news on the network staff told you about
options.nudge: Reading the news on the café's real network is low-risk. Look for the choice that could hand your details to a stranger.

options.text: Check your bank account on mobile data, not Wi-Fi
options.nudge: Mobile data is the safer choice for banking. Look for the choice with a network nobody can vouch for.

cards.explanation: "Free Cafe WiFi 2": the café's second network, which the café has never heard of. It might be a **fake hotspot** set up by a stranger. The café's real network is fine for everyday browsing, and mobile data is best for banking. Tip: turn off auto-join for public networks.
cards.hint: Which network could belong to a stranger instead of the café?

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- Give apps only the **permissions** they need for their job.
- For location, choose **"Only while using the app"**.
- On **public Wi-Fi**, check the network's name. Bank on **mobile data**.

Next module: what to do when something goes wrong.
